This is Sheridan's story, told by the ones who loved her most.

China has spent years aggressively expanding its influence across the Pacific. Now the U.S. is fighting back with a new strategy, one built on trade, investment, and security partnerships instead of foreign aid. Will it be enough to keep America the partner of choice in a region critical to U.S. interests?

Andrew Harding is a Policy Analyst for National Security and Indo-Pacific Affairs at The Heritage Foundation.

One missing word changed everything.

A Spanish court ruling was published, shared online, and quickly transformed into something it never actually said. Within weeks, thousands believed migrants who reached Ceuta could no longer be returned, helping fuel one of the year's most fascinating border crises.

Amine Ghoulidi is a Visiting Fellow at The Heritage Foundation.
